description: Figure 7 is a horizontal stacked bar chart illustrating the average rate at which a model’s attention is most focused on different input segments during generation, broken down into “Context,” “Generated Response,” and “Other (e.g., system prompts).” The category axis is the vertical axis, listing two rows labeled “Ours” (top) and “Standard” (bottom), with no numeric scale shown on this axis. The value axis is the horizontal axis and represents percentage share of attention allocation; it is implicitly linear from 0% to 100% across each full bar, with segment values printed inside the bars rather than shown as tick marks. Each row contains one stacked bar divided into three colored segments according to the legend: blue for “Context,” orange for “Generated Response,” and green for “Other.” For “Ours,” the blue Context segment is labeled 60.6%, the orange Generated Response segment is labeled 31.7%, and the green Other segment is labeled 7.7%. For “Standard,” the blue Context segment is labeled 23.6%, the orange Generated Response segment is labeled 51.1%, and the green Other segment is labeled 25.3%. The bars are not sorted beyond the fixed top-to-bottom order (“Ours” then “Standard”), and there are no additional visual emphases such as outlines or annotations beyond the in-segment percentage labels and the legend.
